messages:
asha_sales: Quick sync — Sylph POC kicks off next week. They have two custom variants (sylph-small-8bit, sylph-large-qat) and want variant orchestration across Dedicated + Hosted fallback. Main asks: compatibility, latency targets, pricing, and security questionnaire. cc @matt_eng @linh_ml @dom_prod

matt_eng: Ok. What's their target QPS and max sequence length? Any custom tokenizer or CUDA ops?

asha_sales: Target ~= 40 qps (batched). p95 latency goals: <220ms for small, <800ms for large. Max seq ~4k. Tokenizer = HF with a small custom vocab. They said no custom CUDA ops initially but might have fused layers in the QAT model.

linh_ml: 4k seq + KV cache will be memory heavy. Large QAT variant may not hit our optimized kernel paths on Ampere/Memory-optimized nodes. We should run a KV/cache memory projection + perf run.

dom_prod: Onboarding plan I propose: 1) compatibility scan (parser + load test) 2) perf profile (batching/latency) 3) quant sweep (8-bit/4-bit) 4) canary on Dedicated then enable Hosted fallback policy. Owners: @matt_eng for scan/profile, @linh_ml for quant tuning, @kevin_sre for infra/keys.

matt_eng: For the scan I'll need: a loader script (minimal), tokenizer files, and weights (or a small synthetic checkpoint). Prefer: s3 link with restricted access. Also share expected input shapes so we can validate KV layout.

asha_sales: I'll ask Sylph for weights + loader + model card and send a secure s3 link. Legal already ok to share under their NDA. Also attaching security questionnaire in next message.

kevin_sre: Quick notes: they require customer-managed KMS for production and audit logs to vendor SIEM. We support BYO KMS in Dedicated and Private; Hosted requires enterprise plan + onboarding ticket. Also data residency: can pin region for Dedicated. I can run cost sim for 2x reserved GPU capacity.

asha_sales: Pricing ask: they want a committed quote for 2x reserved nodes for baseline 40 qps. Any rough ballpark before SRE sim?

dom_prod: Ballpark: small variant on single optimized card ~ "$16k/mo"; large variant that needs multi-card and more memory ~ "$48k/mo" — these are rough. We'll refine after perf profile and batch sim.

linh_ml: Technical blocker to flag: the QAT variant includes RMSNorm changes and some fused attention implementations. If their load script uses a custom op, we may need to implement an adapter or request a non-fused variant. Please ask them to deliver a plain PyTorch load path too.

asha_sales: Noted. I'll request both fused and plain loader. Also they asked about evals — who runs the model-quality regression?

matt_eng: We can run a quick eval harness if they provide a labeled prompt set. Otherwise we run our default regen/sample suite. Include a small eval set with expected outputs to test for regressions.

asha_sales: Security questionnaire attached (will paste answers here). Can someone draft responses focusing on retention, logs, and isolation?

linh_ml: Draft answers: we do not persist customer inputs beyond configured retention windows; KV cache is ephemeral and stored in process/ephemeral storage unless configured; audit logs are retained per enterprise settings and can be exported to their SIEM. I'll write a short paragraph for each section.

kevin_sre: Also include: timeline for KMS onboarding (usually 2-3 weeks), separation of duty for keys, and SOC2 controls pointer. I'll add infra-specific details.

asha_sales: Timeline summary to Sylph: ask for artifacts today, expect weights + loaders by EOD Mon, compatibility + perf scans Tue-Wed, quant sweep Thu, canary on Dedicated by end of week pending scan results. Is everyone ok?

matt_eng: Ack. I'll queue the scan and reserve time Tue/Wed.

linh_ml: Ack. I'll prep quant sweep templates and run initial 8-bit test as soon as we have the checkpoint.

kevin_sre: I'll start cost sim and prep KMS ticket draft.

deploybot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance Thu 02:00-04:00 UTC (Hosted) — may affect fallback testing. :warning:

asha_sales: Thanks all — I'll update this thread with the S3 link + SQ answers when I have them. :pray:
